To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Philippine agricultural sector will continue to grow, but that the growth rate will decline over the next decade.

(a) Philippine agriculture is likely to continue growing at a moderate pace, with rice production increasing dramatically, (b) per capita consumption of food items is expected to continue increasing, and (c) the alternative policy scenario involving liberalization and re-allocating expenditure support to export-oriented agricultural sub-sectors would result in lower prices for rice and meat products, higher per capita consumption of rice, and faster increases in consumption of other food items.

Philippine agricultural growth is likely to continue, but with substantial increases in the prices of meat, rice and poultry products, and with the need for substantial importation of rice, maize, and poultry products.

the Philippines is a country with an agriculture sector which is still very much dependent on the government and its policies.
, in the long run, the benefits of trade reform outweigh the costs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Philippines should continue with the outward-oriented policy and should not revert to the protectionism and import-substitution policy.

, while the business-as-usual policy regime would be able to meet the food requirements of a growing population, it would be at the expense of higher food prices and a less competitive agricultural sector.
, in the long run, a more open and outward-oriented policy would be better for the Philippines.

the Philippine agricultural sector is poised for significant growth, with the potential for a major boost if the right policies are in place.
the current policy regime is not sustainable.

the Philippines has an opportunity to reap the benefits of a more liberal and competitive agricultural sector, but only if it can overcome its historical aversion toward trade liberalization and embrace a more outward-oriented policy.
